sn1.60:1.1: This short discourse serves for the Buddha to articulate a naturalistic theory of poetry.
sn1.60:2.1: Rig Veda 10.90.9 says that verses, chants, and metres were born from the sacrifice.
sn1.60:2.2: The _akkhara_ (“syllable”) is the smallest indivisible morpheme, typically consisting of a consonant bound with a vowel. Mystically, it is the “imperishable” Divinity within all things.
sn1.60:2.3: Chāndogya Upaniṣad 7.1.4 defines “name” (_nāma_) as the Vedic texts and sciences.
sn1.60:2.4: The Buddha deliberately uses the worldly word for “poet” (_kavi_) instead of the divinely-inspired Vedic “seer” (_isi_, Sanskrit _ṛṣi_).
